title: ReasoningTrace-Eval: A Multi-hop Reasoning Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models Based on Structured Faithfulness
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computational Intelligence
abstract: To address the pervasive "correctness by fluke" phenomenon in multi-hop reasoning evaluations—where Large Language Models (LLMs) yield correct answers via factual errors or logical leaps—this paper proposes ReasoningTrace-Eval, an automated evaluation framework. Inspired by the pedagogical principle of prioritizing the reasoning process over final outcomes, this framework transcends traditional answer-matching paradigms in favor of a structured, interpretable process-oriented verification.Specifically, the framework leverages prompt engineering to decompose natural language reasoning chains into sequences of knowledge triples, establishing verifiable intermediate logical representations. A DeBERTaV3 model, optimized via gradient disentanglement, is then employed to perform fine-grained contextual consistency verification for each triple. Metrics such as Triple Faithfulness Rate and Hallucination Density are introduced to enable precise hallucination localization and process diagnostics. Experimental results across multi-hop benchmarks, including HotpotQA and MuSiQue, demonstrate a significant correlation with human judgment (average Spearman ρ=0.542). Notably, ReasoningTrace-Eval robustly identifies "fluke" samples overlooked by conventional metrics, revealing an overestimation of reasoning capabilities by up to 27.2% across various models. This work establishes a new paradigm for reliable reasoning evaluation and provides a foundation for developing transparent, trustworthy next-generation AI systems.
